title: Worked Great for Nine Months, Then Burned Out
text:
Worked Great for Nine Months, Then Burned Out. This NINJA 12-CUP PROGRAMMABLE COFFEE MAKER (with Classic and Rich Brews, 60 oz. Water Reservoir, and Thermal Flavor Extraction (CE201), Black/Stainless Steel) made excellent coffee for me for about 9 months. My household drinks a lot of coffee, so the coffee maker was used for an average of two pots per day.

Today, I made a second pot and left the carafe on the warming plate as usual. An hour or so later, the coffee maker began softly beeping. It seemed to have spontaneously attempted to brew another pot of coffee--but of course the water reservoir was empty.

The pot smelled hot, like something was wrong with the electrical parts. I tried turning the coffee maker off and on, but the beeping persisted. Ditto after I unplugged the coffee maker and turned it on again.

Obviously the coffee maker is now unsafe to use, even if the beeping stops after the coffee maker cools down. There is nothing in the instruction booklet about this steady, soft beeping warning. I’m glad that the beeping alerted me to a problem, but I wonder what would have happened if I hadn’t been home when it started up.

Unfortunately, I liked this coffee maker so much, I purchased a backup. I still plan to use the backup, but I will be afraid to leave it plugged in or turned on when I’m not close by. This is an issue, because unplugging the coffee maker cancels the programming, and turning it off cancels the stay warm feature.

I will NOT be purchasing another of these expensive coffee makers. Because the pot was so heavily used, I can accept a 9-month lifespan. But all of my other coffee makers have simply stopped working when they were worn out. This one was burning out, with some kind of electrical malfunction.
